name: office_corridor_loop
notes: Hand-written route for the office corridor, validated against the world's collision geometry
by sim/isaac/tools/check_drive_path.py: 29.9 m in 106.7 s, worst clearance 0.54 m, which is
the scene's own spawn pose -- nothing here is tighter than where the car starts.
Edit the segments freely, then re-run the check before driving:
sim/isaac/tools/check_drive_path.py --segments sim/isaac/config/routes/office_corridor_loop.json
THERE IS NO RETURN LEG, AND THAT IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT AN OVERSIGHT. The first version drove
back up in reverse. It diverged: the checker predicted x = 17.03 at the bottom of the descent
and the real car was at x = 17.47 -- 0.44 m of open-loop drift over 10 m. At y = -8 the free
lane ends at x = 17.76, so with a 0.30 m footprint the car was scraping the east wall, and a
car pushing a wall goes to NaN. The drift (0.44 m) is simply larger than the slack the pinch
leaves (0.25 m): an open-loop segment list can do the descent but cannot do the return.
Driving back needs feedback on the lateral position, not a longer list of segments.
Three more things the checker taught us, each of which had broken an earlier attempt:
1. A U-TURN DOES NOT FIT EITHER. The corridor is 1-2 m wide and a U-turn displaces the car
sideways by twice the turn radius (2.07 m); the lane 2 m west is walled at y = -8.
2. THE CAR DOES NOT SPAWN ON THE CENTRELINE. At y = -1 the widest point is x = 17.10 with
only 0.65 m, and the car spawns at x = 16.814 where that pinch leaves 0.35 m. `shift_east`
moves it ~0.21 m east, which buys 0.55 m both going down and coming back.
3. THE LOOP CLOSES ON THE ORIGINAL HEADING. 22.0 s over-rotated by 5.3 deg; 21.7 s lands at
-90.5 deg. That mattered for the old return leg and is kept because a closed loop is the
honest way to end up where the graph says you are.
The 360 degree loops sit in the wide pocket at y = -11 (2.0-2.7 m of room). They are there to
give Hydra views in every direction from one place, which is what builds rooms instead of a
ribbon of places. The SECOND loop is the revisit the return leg was meant to provide: the same
space seen again from every angle, which is where you find out whether Hydra re-observes what
it already mapped or quietly duplicates it. Watch whether PLACES keeps climbing during
`loop_again` or levels off -- levelling off is the good answer.
speed m/s (negative = reverse), steer rad (positive = toward +x; limits +0.31975/-0.30935),
dur = sim seconds.
